Hi Ethan,

Thanks again for taking the demo today, really appreciated the time and the detailed walkthrough of the Acme ingestion/use-case. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goal: validate model fit for Acme's QA+agent workflow focusing on function/tool calling (inventory lookup, price calculation) and structured JSON output (order schema v2).
- Deliverables we discussed: baseline eval report (accuracy, schema compliance rate, generation latency), recommended model/configs, prompt set we used, and a short-run of retries/partial-failure handling.
- Timeline: initial baseline run in 3 business days (target 2026-08-25), follow-up sync the week after with results.

Action items for you: please confirm the top 3 priority scenarios we should evaluate (e.g., price calc, inventory check, returns processing) and upload any representative sample payloads (anonymized) if possible. I've attached the prompt set we used in the demo and a stubbed eval.csv we'll populate.

Attachments: prompt-set-acme.jsonl (prompt examples), acme-eval-results-v1.csv (eval stub)

Related links: HubSpot ACME-12345 (I linked the record) and a Drive folder where we'll drop results.

If that timeline works I'll kick off the baseline runs and loop in Aditya for model recommendations / quantization considerations.

Best,

Ethan,

Great, thanks for confirming the scenarios. We got the sample payloads in the Drive folder (confirmed). Quick answers and next steps: 

- JSON schema compliance: yes, we run schema validation as part of the eval harness. Outputs are validated against your order schema v2 and we report a per-example pass/fail plus a categorized error (missing field, type mismatch, extra fields, malformed JSON).
- Retries & idempotency for tool calls: our baseline strategy for the pilot is: 1) function-calling first attempt; 2) if the model produces malformed or missing function call, we run a single deterministic retry with a clarified prompt (we capture the retry and mark it in the audit); 3) if the retry still fails, we surface as 'agent error' and optionally fall back to a safe default or flag for human review depending on the policy you pick. We'll include counts for first-call success, retry-success, and failure.

Attached: prompt-set-acme.jsonl (the set we'll test) and redwood-model-recommendations.pdf (high-level picks for the pilot).

Proposed timeline: baseline run (3 business days) -> internal review -> 30-min sync week of 2026-08-31 to review results. For procurement, I'll send a short SOW template + pilot estimate (cc'd Neha who owns pricing).

Let me know if you want us to enable stricter schema enforcement (hard-fail) vs. permissive logging — default is permissive with per-example flags.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Post-demo: Model fit & tool-calling evals for Acme - next steps (technical recs)

Looping in a short technical recommendation for the baseline runs: 

Recommended models/configs (pilot - balance of quality vs latency):
- RW-13B-instruct (fp16) - best baseline for structured JSON + instruction-following; expect high schema compliance with moderate latency.
- RW-7B-q4_0 - low-latency quantized candidate for throughput-sensitive routes (good for real-time inventory checks).
- RW-70B-instruct - high-quality model if you want max correctness for price-calculation edge cases; expect higher latency/cost.

Prompting & function-calling guidance:
- Use explicit function schemas for inventory_lookup and calculate_price with strict parameter typing.
- Add an example in the prompt-set that demonstrates an edge-case discount + tax calculation.
- For structured output, include a clear preface: "Return ONLY JSON matching order_schema_v2. If you cannot populate a field, return null for that field."

JSON schema compliance & validation approach:
- Run a JSON parse + jsonschema validation step on every model response.
- Classify failures into: parse_error, type_mismatch, missing_required, extra_fields. Produce per-example diagnostics and an aggregated compliance rate.
- Track first-call success %, retry-success % (retry uses clarified prompt with stricter instructions), and final-fail % (flag for human review).

Retry strategy & idempotency:
- Single automated deterministic retry for parse errors or missing function_call; include a copy of the original prompt + an instruction to strictly follow the schema.
- If a function call is invoked twice due to retries, mark as idempotent attempt. Recommend that Acme's API surface an idempotency key (request_id) to make server-side handling safe.

Benchmarks & metrics to capture:
- Schema compliance rate (primary), field-level accuracy for numeric outputs (e.g., tax calc), latency p50/p95, tokens per call, first-call success vs retry-success, and cost estimate (tokens * model cost).

Quantization/throughput notes:
- For the low-latency path use RW-7B-q4_0 with continuous batching and KV cache for repeated session context; expect 2-3x cost reduction vs fp16 with modest accuracy delta.

Attachments & links: prompt-set-acme.jsonl, acme-eval-results-v1.csv (we'll populate), redwood-model-recommendations.pdf; internal eval dashboard will be posted to the Drive folder and linked to HubSpot ACME-12345.

If you want, I can run a quick 500-sample smoke test against inventory_lookup and price calculation today to validate the pipeline.

Aditya
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
